AVDTune creates its own app registration 'AVDTune' (or reuses the one it created and saved before, after checking it) (public client, http://localhost, no secret), grants the admin consent for the permissions above and then signs you in with it. stage.signin.intro: One normal Microsoft sign-in in an embedded window: you sign in yourself. AVDTune gets four tokens from it, one for Microsoft Graph, one for the SharePoint site, one for Azure Resource Manager and one for Azure Storage (the NTFS rows of the FSLogix check; optional, an older app registration without it signs in without that token and says so). Microsoft puts every consented permission of a resource into its token, so both Graph tokens carry all Graph permissions listed here; extra permissions are reported as a warning. The tokens live in memory only and are removed on closing, on sign out and by Finish.

stage.snap.intro: One snapshot per image version: before AVDTune changes the master there must be a finished snapshot of its OS disk from after the last change of the previous version and before the first change of this one. A snapshot made after the last change (the current state) counts too, so Create snapshot now is always usable; a rollback goes back to the start of the version or to that current state. Create one here (incremental, named by the pattern of this environment) or choose an existing one, then confirm it with your first and last name. When AVDTune already changed the master in this version, choose a snapshot from the start of the version or one made after the last change; snapshots that do not count are grey with the reason. Until then every page is read only.

The rollback goes back to the state of the snapshot: the start of the version (everything done in this version since then is gone) or, for a snapshot of the current state, to that state, so note what was done in the protocol first.
